title: Incident Response — In Flight, Waiting On A Human
description: A live run captured mid-flight: four nodes done, one probe failed, one result served from cache, the mitigation gate currently waiting on a human, and the rollback path still unreached. Cycles are real here — the hypothesis loop ran three times before it landed.

nodes.name: Incident commander
nodes.description: Holds the incident state. Fans out evidence gathering in parallel, then drives the hypothesis loop and decides when a human needs to be involved.
nodes.prompt:
You are incident commander for a live P1.

Gather evidence in parallel before forming any hypothesis. Do not propose a mitigation until a hypothesis has survived a falsification attempt against real telemetry. Any mitigation that touches production requires human approval — never apply one yourself.
nodes.output:
Evidence plan, all three in parallel:
  · service telemetry for checkout-api and its 4 dependencies
  · structured logs for the alert window
  · distributed traces for slow requests

Then: hypothesise, falsify, repeat until one survives. Human approves before anything is applied.

nodes.name: Form hypothesis
nodes.description: Proposes a cause consistent with all available evidence. Ran three times — the first two were falsified and fed back in as exclusions.
nodes.logs:
round 1  "payments-svc deploy at 03:09 introduced a slow query"
         falsified — no deploy in the window, last release was 41h ago
round 2  "organic traffic spike saturating the pool"
         falsified — RPS is within 4% of the trailing 7-day median for this hour
round 3  "connection leak: pool grows without release"
         survived falsification
nodes.output:
Hypothesis (round 3): payments-svc is leaking postgres connections.

Support:
  · pool at 198/200 with 194 active, 41 waiters
  · active connection count rises monotonically from 03:11, never recovers
  · no deploy, no traffic anomaly — rules out the two obvious causes
  · leak rate ≈ 8 connections/min, consistent with one un-released connection per
    failed fraud-svc callback, and fraud-svc callbacks started erroring at 03:10

Predicts: restarting payments-svc pods returns the pool to baseline within 60s.

findings.observation: Postgres primary connection pool at 198/200 saturation due to unreleased connections during fraud-svc callback timeouts.
findings.pushbackReason: Rounds 1 and 2 falsified: no deploy occurred in 41h, and organic traffic is within 4% of 7-day median.
findings.opposedChanges: Unsafe direct pod restart without connection draining.
findings.remediation: Drain connections on payments-svc, restart pod pool, and patch connection release in exception handler.

evidence: Pool active connections projected to drop from 194 to 12

nodes.name: Falsify hypothesis
nodes.description: Actively tries to break the current hypothesis against telemetry rather than confirm it. This is what rejected rounds one and two.
nodes.output:
Round 3 survives.

Tried and failed to break it:
  · if it were load, RPS would correlate — it does not (r = 0.04)
  · if it were a slow query, mean query time would rise — it is flat at 3.1ms
  · if it were the pool sizing, waiters would appear at every peak — they never have before

One caveat: without traces I cannot prove the leak is on the fraud-svc callback path
specifically. Confidence: high on the leak, medium on the exact call site.

nodes.name: Approve mitigation
nodes.description: Waiting on the on-call engineer. Proposed action is a rolling restart of payments-svc, which drops in-flight checkout requests.
nodes.prompt:
Proposed mitigation: rolling restart of payments-svc (6 pods, 2 at a time).

Expected effect: connection pool returns to baseline within 60s of the last pod cycling.
Expected cost: in-flight checkout requests on restarted pods fail; roughly 40-90 requests
based on current RPS. Client retries should absorb most of them.

Confidence: high on the leak, medium on the exact call site (no traces available).
Reversible: yes — this is a restart, not a config or code change.

Approve / reject / request another hypothesis round.
